idea: RutaLeche Peru is an offline-first mobile app that uses machine learning to optimize milk collection routes for Peruvian dairy cooperatives and processing plants.

selected_gap.title: Offline-First Mobile App for Remote Milk Collection
selected_gap.pain: Rural areas lack reliable internet, making real-time optimization useless and forcing drivers to rely on paper and memory, leading to delays and errors.
selected_gap.why_now: Smartphone penetration is high in rural Peru; offline sync technology is mature and can bridge the connectivity gap.
selected_gap.evidence_needed: Test offline-capable MVP with drivers in remote regions and compare on-time collection and data accuracy against manual methods.
selected_gap.risk: Infrastructure may improve faster than expected; offline sync adds development complexity and maintenance overhead.

Peruvian dairy collection market estimated at ~$50M TAM; niche but not massive.

Generic route optimizers exist but lack offline-first and milk-specific features; manual methods are the main alternative.
Unknown founder motivation; assumed moderate personal connection to problem.
High smartphone penetration and mature offline-sync tech make this newly feasible.
Similar offline-first logistics tools have succeeded in other regions (e.g., India), but not directly analogous.
No signal of long-term commitment from founder; assumed moderate.
Potential to expand to other perishables and regions in Latin America.
Narrow wedge in a large, underserved market with clear need for digitization.

vc_rubric_scores.rationale: No detailed team background; assumed relevant but not proven.
Peru dairy collection TAM ~$50M; growth moderate but timing right.
Offline ML on basic smartphones is a defensible moat given domain data.
No evidence of users, pilots, or revenue; purely conceptual.
No defined pricing or unit economics; LTV:CAC and margins unknown.
Incumbents are manual; generic route apps lack offline and domain fit.
No financial details; burn rate and runway unknown.
Realistic failure mode: connectivity improves or incumbents add offline features.

decision: Proceed with caution, focusing on rapid MVP testing with real drivers in a single cooperative.
next_experiments: Recruit 3-5 dairy drivers in one remote valley to test offline MVP for 2 weeks; measure on-time collection rate vs manual baseline.
Conduct structured interviews to assess willingness to pay $10-$20/month per driver.
Evaluate technical feasibility of offline ML inference on low-end Android phones (e.g., RAM usage, battery drain).
kill_criteria: Less than 50% of drivers use the app consistently after 4 weeks.
On-time collection rate improves by less than 5% over manual methods.
Unable to achieve stable offline model performance on target devices.
_iteration_one_liner: We optimize milk collection routes for Peruvian dairy cooperatives and plants using an offline-first mobile app with machine learning.
